clue.text: Suit one into heavy breathing, as produced by impulsive strokes?

parts.note: a suit at law is a legal action

indicators.note: one is put into the heavy breathing, so it goes inside that word

parts.note: heavy breathing is panting
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone panting heavily while trying on a suit, oddly linked to sudden strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints PRINTING, but the wordplay (I inside PANTING) and the definition both give PAINTING; the eighth letter is unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Action painting, the style of Pollock, is made by flinging and dripping paint in impulsive gestures across the canvas.

clue.text: Wouldn't you say that girl's Candy (a streetwalker as the song goes on to reveal)

definitions.text: Wouldn't you say that girl's Candy (a streetwalker as the song goes on to reveal)

parts.words: Wouldn't you say that girl's Candy (a streetwalker as the song goes on to reveal)
parts.note: a folksy 'wouldn't you say' question plus 'that girl is candy', i.e. sugary, names an old popular song whose lyric goes on to watch her walking down the street

explanation.surface: A coy remark about a girl called Candy, with a nudge that she walks the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1927 song asks this question and continues 'see her coming down the street', so the setter's 'streetwalker' is a playful misreading of its lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paraphrases the title line of a 1920s standard, asking whether the girl is sweet like candy.

clue.text: Material wife stifled by archaic husband

indicators.note: the wife is smothered by the husband word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: to husband land once meant to cultivate or till it

explanation.surface: A wife smothered by an old-fashioned husband, with material as the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a man but is the old verb meaning to cultivate soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs, so it is a material.

clue.text: Science that might lead to spectacular improvement of runabout-type motor

definitions.text: Science that might lead to spectacular improvement

indicators.note: a runabout gets the letters running about into a new order

explanation.surface: Some engineering science that turns a runabout's motor into something spectacular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runabout' looks like a small car but signals an anagram of TYPE MOTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye testing leads to spectacles, so the improvement is spectacular in the eyeglass sense.

clue.text: Article about tips of roots in seed vegetable

indicators.note: the article-plus-tips group goes inside the seed word

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

indicators.note: the article goes around the tips of roots

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for growing a root vegetable from seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips of' gives the first and last letters of 'roots'; 'seed' looks like part of 'seed vegetable' but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root crop eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Brummie's — too old for love", lay-it-on-thick technique

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so Brummie's means I'm
past it means too old
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being past romance, then mentions thick-painting technique.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; here 'Brummie's' is 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of applying paint in thick layers.

clue.text: One not easily giving up rank without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so rank goes around resistance

parts.note: a tier is a rank or row
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps trying and never drops rank, even without opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like minus but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who keeps trying, a persistent person.

clue.text: New Blairite movement for the anxious type

indicators.note: a movement of letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: The New Labour movement as followed by a nervous supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' and 'Blairite' evoke New Labour; 'movement' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biter is a nervous person, from the anxious habit of biting nails.

clue.text: Aphetic smear of negative 'elp

parts.note: no is a negative
help with an H dropped suggests hint said the same way, 'int

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch plea for help sounding like a smear.
explanation.walkthrough: Aphetic means losing an initial letter: NOINT is anoint without its A, and the 'elp clue drops the H of hint likewise.
explanation.definitionFit: Noint is an aphetic form of anoint, meaning to smear with oil.

clue.text: Monitor's class pet, rail-touring round Italy

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the letter for Italy
touring sends the letters wandering into a new order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A pet lizard taken on a rail tour round Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' scrambles PET RAIL into REPTLIA, and 'round' puts that around I. 'Monitor' looks like a class prefect but is the lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor lizard belongs to the class of reptiles, Latin name Reptilia.

clue.text: With Watson, he unravelled a great scientific mystery (created by crime writer, C. Heap)

definitions.text: With Watson, he unravelled a great scientific mystery

parts.note: Dick Francis was a writer of racing crime novels
C is taken as written
a rick is a stack or heap of hay

explanation.surface: A great scientific mystery solved, written up like a detective story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C. Heap' looks like an author's name but supplies C and RICK.
explanation.definitionFit: The structure of DNA was discovered by James Watson with this scientist in 1953.

clue.text: Wise ruler not accompanied by second knight

parts.note: solo means unaccompanied
mo is a short moment
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A wise king left alone except for a knight for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for his wisdom.

clue.text: One who scores in bed, reserve outwardly rejected

indicators.note: the reversed reserve lies on the outside of the bed
rejected turns the reserve word back

parts.note: a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Someone scoring in bed while the reserve is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns RES into SER, which 'outwardly' sets around CRIB; 'scores' suggests sex or sport but means scratching lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A scriber is a pointed tool used to score lines on wood or metal.

clue.text: Dead easy to be a settler abroad

parts.note: ex means former, as a dead thing is past
pat means glib or easy, as in a pat answer

explanation.surface: Settling abroad is dead easy.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat lives outside their native country, settled abroad.

clue.text: Partly emptied old Marina, fixed ignition problem

indicators.note: emptied removes the middle, leaving the first and last letters
fixed means repaired, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An old Morris Marina, partly gutted and fixed, with ignition trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: PY (Partly emptied) then O + MARINA rearranged as ROMANIA. A Marina was a 1970s British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to start fires, so a problem with igniting things.

clue.text: Hormone for South American type outside clubs

parts.note: pro means for, in favour

indicators.note: the Latin goes outside the clubs letter

parts.note: a Latin is a Latin American
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A hormone sold to a South American dancer outside the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolactin is the pituitary hormone that stimulates milk production.

clue.text: Ancient god raised to transform large place in Russia

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ra was the ancient Egyptian sun god
to change is to transform

explanation.surface: An ancient god lifted up to transform something large.
explanation.walkthrough: AR (Ra raised) + CHANGE + L; the place is the port city also called Arkhangelsk.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel is the English name of Arkhangelsk, a port city in northern Russia.

clue.text: One always prepared to bother with capsized tug — awfully sorry about it

indicators.note: the sorry anagram goes about the tug
awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled
a capsized boat is upside down, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A capsized tug and a captain awfully sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges SORRY into ORRYS; 'capsized' gives GUT; 'about' sets ORRYS around GUT, with W in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A worryguts is someone who habitually frets, always ready to worry.

clue.text: Endure less than try

parts.note: under means less than
a go is a try

explanation.surface: Putting up with less than an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to experience or endure something unpleasant.

clue.text: Look promising and build towards a centre

parts.note: to shape is to build or form
up means towards a city or university, as in going up to London

explanation.surface: Looking hopeful and building towards a central point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is used in British English for travelling towards a capital or major city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shape up means to develop well or look promising.

clue.text: Barker's — Phwoar! Good one!"

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of admiration like phwoar
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dog owner exclaiming admiringly at a fine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker's' is 'Barker is'. Cor and phwoar are British exclamations of admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a dog, and dogs bark, so a barker.

clue.text: In the royal habit of, um, getting exploited?

parts.note: er is a hesitation like um
mined means dug for and exploited

explanation.surface: A hesitant question about being exploited in royal robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means wearing ermine fur, the trim of royal robes.

clue.text: Upstart star put before King Kim, the old star

indicators.note: the star goes before the king

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares up
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A rising star placed ahead of a king, recalling an old film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Novak is a Hollywood actress, star of Vertigo in the 1950s.

clue.text: The language when one has to drive home! Agents taken aback!

parts.note: A means one
to ram something home is to drive it in

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Someone has to drive home and agents are startled.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language spoken in the Near East.

clue.text: Threatening behaviour of one taking drink back to front

parts.note: A means one

indicators.note: the last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or drink generally

explanation.surface: Someone drinking and turning aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: GROG with its back letter G sent to the front gives GGRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, threatening behaviour.

clue.text: All there is of a familiar place to learn lines?

parts.note: uni is the familiar short form of university
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Wondering about a place to learn lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all existing matter and space.

clue.text: Line taken by musical tenor

indicators.note: the line is taken into the musical

parts.note: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical

explanation.surface: A tenor delivering a line in a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a famous Italian operatic tenor.

clue.text: Michael, fool, has love for one drippy artist

parts.note: Michael Jackson the pop star

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so the love letter replaces the one letter in the fool word

parts.note: pillock is British slang for a fool
I is one
love is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The pop star Michael, a fool in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock made paintings by dripping paint onto canvas.
